jobs.label: DEER MEAT
jobs.design: One boneless lean elongated haunch pickup, a low rounded asymmetric wedge of rich cranberry-red meat. The left end in FRONT0 is broad and blunt, the right end tapers smoothly but stays thick. Length about twice width, thickness about one-third width. No full cream rim: only one thin continuous cream seam along the FRONT broad side just below the top edge, and one small oval cream fat spot on top near the blunt LEFT end. Broad subtly sculpted planes, no fine marbling. This silhouette must be a lean tapering haunch, clearly different from a round steak or rectangular processed meat block. Zero bones. FIXED ORBIT: FRONT0 blunt end screenLEFT/taper screenRIGHT; FRONT RIGHT45 taper near lowerRIGHT/blunt far upperLEFT; RIGHT90 direct taper end; REAR RIGHT135 taper near lowerLEFT/blunt far upperRIGHT; REAR180 taper screenLEFT/blunt screenRIGHT, front cream seam hidden; REAR LEFT225 blunt near lowerRIGHT/taper far upperLEFT, front seam hidden; LEFT270 direct blunt end; FRONT LEFT315 blunt near lowerLEFT/taper far upperRIGHT, cream seam visible. Top fat spot remains at blunt end in every panel.

jobs.label: BOAR MEAT
jobs.design: One thick raw bone-in chop pickup with a broad rounded triangular/teardrop silhouette, salmon-red muscle and a thick cream fat cap along the REAR long edge only. At FRONT0 the left end is broad, the right end is slightly narrower. ONE small oval cream bone cross-section lies flush in the TOP face near the narrow RIGHT end, containing one small warm beige marrow center; never add a projecting bone, second bone or extra piece. The top muscle has only one broad shallow curved groove near the broad left end. Soft chunky edges and sculpted broad planes. It is a thick chop, not thin generic steak or ham leg. Keep ONE oval bone, ONE rear fat cap and ONE top groove anatomically simplified and fixed as the object rotates.

jobs.label: RABBIT MEAT
jobs.design: A small paired saddle-portion pickup: exactly TWO separate boneless smooth blush-red rounded oblong pieces, parallel along the left-right long axis, side by side front-to-back, close but with a visible narrow gap. The FRONT piece is slightly longer and thicker; the REAR piece is about80% its length. Their left ends are rounded, right ends gently tapered. Each piece has exactly ONE simple thin cream seam running along its top length; no extra bones, no full fat rims, no third piece. Treat the two pieces as one rigid arranged resource unit: same gap and same fore/aft order from every angle, never rearrange. FRONT0 shows longer front piece partly occluding the smaller rear piece; FRONT RIGHT45 shows tapered RIGHT ends nearer lowerRIGHT; RIGHT90 shows two tapered ends side by side in depth-projected arrangement; REAR RIGHT135 tapered ends nearer lowerLEFT; REAR180 smaller rear piece now nearer viewer, longer behind; REAR LEFT225 rounded LEFT ends nearer lowerRIGHT; LEFT270 looks directly at two rounded left ends; FRONT LEFT315 rounded LEFT ends nearer lowerLEFT. 45/225 share top-left to bottom-right long-axis diagonal;135/315 share bottom-left to top-right diagonal. Maintain exact two-piece count and physically coherent overlaps. Gentle broad stylized meat material, clearly smaller/finer than deer or boar yet comfortably sized within panels.
